idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Why a Toilet Keeps Running: Flapper Seal vs. Overflow Line
description: When a toilet runs continuously, water is escaping the tank through one of two primary pathways. Most commonly, the rubber flapper at the bottom of the tank has hardened, warped, or accumulated mineral buildup, preventing a complete seal against the flush valve seat. As water leaks past the flapper into the bowl, the tank level drops, forcing the fill valve to run indefinitely. Alternatively, if the fill valve float is set too high, water will continuously spill over the top of the overflow tube. Inspecting whether water is trickling past the flapper or rising over the overflow tube immediately identifies the failed component.
image_prompt: A clean 9:16 vertical educational cutaway illustration of a modern ceramic toilet tank showing its internal components in crisp detail. Inside the clear cutaway view, highlight the fill valve, overflow tube, floating cup mechanism, and the rubber flapper sitting on the flush valve seat at the bottom of the tank. Show a subtle blue water flow trickling past a slightly lifted flapper edge into the drain channel below. Bright neutral studio lighting, realistic ceramic, plastic, and rubber material textures. Professional plumbing textbook visual, vertical composition with uncluttered top and bottom areas for text overlay. No text, no labels, no arrows, no logos, no watermarks.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear cutaway of a toilet tank to isolate the two main mechanical failure points causing continuous water flow. Viewers immediately see the relationship between the flapper seal at the bottom and the overflow tube in the center. Visualizing the water escaping beneath the flapper helps apprentices and homeowners understand why the fill valve never turns off.

on_image_text.hook: Why Your Toilet Won't Stop Running
on_image_text.explanation: A degraded flapper seal constantly leaks water into the bowl, preventing the tank from staying full.
on_image_text.takeaway: Check if water is seeping past the flapper before replacing the fill valve.
